claim: Brugia malayi represents a leading cause of disability in the developing world, causing lymphatic filariasis in nearly 40 million people.
source: The filarial nematode Brugia malayi represents a leading cause of disability in the developing world, causing lymphatic filariasis in nearly 40 million people.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about the disease burden of lymphatic filariasis.

claim: Currently available drugs are not well-suited to mass drug administration efforts for lymphatic filariasis.
source: Currently available drugs are not well-suited to mass drug administration efforts, so new treatments are urgently required.
evidence: This claim is supported by inference from the limitations of current treatments discussed in the manuscript.

claim: The endosymbiotic bacteria Wolbachia is vital to the filarial worm.
source: One potential vulnerability is the endosymbiotic bacteria Wolbachia—present in many filariae—which is vital to the worm.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on Wolbachia's role in filarial nematodes.

claim: iDC625 is the first compartmentalized metabolic model of a parasitic worm.
source: Here, we present iDC625, the first compartmentalized metabolic model of a parasitic worm.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract and represents a primary finding of the study.

claim: The model predicts a set of 102 reactions essential to the survival of B. malayi.
source: We used this model to show how metabolic pathway usage allows the worm to adapt to different environments, and predict a set of 102 reactions essential to the survival of B. malayi.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational modeling data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Three predicted essential reactions were validated with drug tests demonstrating novel antifilarial properties.
source: We validated three of those reactions with drug tests and demonstrated novel antifilarial properties for all three compounds.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental drug testing data presented in the manuscript.

claim: As of 2015, an estimated 38.8 million people had lymphatic filariasis.
source: As of 2015, an estimated 38.8 million people had lymphatic filariasis with an estimated 1 billion people at risk in 72 endemic countries (Vos and GBD 2015 Disease and Injury Incidence and Prevalence Collaborators, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to an epidemiological study.

claim: An estimated 1 billion people are at risk for lymphatic filariasis in 72 endemic countries.
source: As of 2015, an estimated 38.8 million people had lymphatic filariasis with an estimated 1 billion people at risk in 72 endemic countries (Vos and GBD 2015 Disease and Injury Incidence and Prevalence Collaborators, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to an epidemiological study.

claim: Lymphatic filariasis is caused by Brugia malayi, Brugia timori, and Wuchereria bancrofti.
source: One of the most debilitating is lymphatic filariasis (LF)—also called elephantiasis—which is caused by Brugia malayi, Brugia timori, and Wuchereria bancrofti.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge about the causative agents of lymphatic filariasis.

claim: Microfilariae are transmitted by mosquitoes during blood meals.
source: Transmission occurs when microfilariae released by a female worm within an infected individual circulate in the blood where they are ingested by one of several species of mosquito.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about the transmission cycle of filarial nematodes.

claim: Infective third-stage filarial larvae (L3) are transmitted to a mammalian host by penetrating the bite wound during mosquito blood meals.
source: In the insect vector, the larvae undergo development; during subsequent blood meals, infective third-stage filarial larvae (L3) are transmitted to a mammalian host by penetrating the bite wound.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about the transmission cycle of filarial nematodes.

claim: Current mass drug administration efforts for lymphatic filariasis involve diethylcarbamazine, ivermectin, and albendazole.
source: Current mass drug administration efforts involve a small selection of drugs—diethylcarbamazine, ivermectin, and albendazole—with limited effectiveness against the adult stages of the parasites.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about current treatment strategies.

claim: Diethylcarbamazine, ivermectin, and albendazole have limited effectiveness against the adult stages of filarial parasites.
source: Current mass drug administration efforts involve a small selection of drugs—diethylcarbamazine, ivermectin, and albendazole—with limited effectiveness against the adult stages of the parasites.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about the limitations of current antifilarial drugs.

claim: Treatment for lymphatic filariasis must continue for the lifespan of the adult worms, which can be up to 15 years.
source: To prevent transmission and to relieve symptoms, treatment must continue for the lifespan of the adult worms, which can be up to 15 years (Molyneux et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research on the lifespan of adult filarial worms.

claim: Diethylcarbamazine is contraindicated in regions where Onchocerca volvulus or Loa loa are endemic.
source: Furthermore, diethylcarbamazine is contraindicated in regions where Onchocerca volvulus or Loa loa—other filarial nematodes—are endemic (Gyapong et al., 2005; Taylor et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on drug contraindications.

claim: Ivermectin is contraindicated in regions where L. loa is co-endemic due to potential life-threatening complications.
source: Ivermectin is also contraindicated in regions where L. loa is co-endemic due to potential life-threatening complications (Gardon et al., 1997; Boussinesq et al., 1998; Boussinesq et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on ivermectin complications.

claim: Emergence of resistance to diethylcarbamazine, ivermectin, and albendazole has been reported in filarial nematodes.
source: While anthelmintic resistance has not yet manifested as a serious treatment issue in humans as it has in veterinary medicine (Kaplan and Vidyashankar, 2012), the potential remains a serious threat; emergence of resistance in these species against diethylcarbamazine (Eberhard et al., 1991), ivermectin (Awadzi et al., 2004; Eng et al., 2006), and albendazole (Schwab et al., 2005) has been reported for many years.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on anthelmintic resistance.

claim: Wolbachia bacteria are essential for adult worm fitness and reproduction.
source: These bacteria are from the genus Wolbachia, specific to each helminth, and found to be essential for adult worm fitness and reproduction (Taylor et al., 2013b).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research on Wolbachia's role in filarial nematodes.

claim: Targeting Wolbachia with doxycycline reduces Wolbachia numbers, sterilizes adult females, and reduces symptoms of lymphatic filariasis.
source: Targeting these bacteria with the antibiotic doxycycline was shown to reduce numbers of Wolbachia present in the worms, sterilize adult females, and reduce symptoms of lymphatic filariasis (Debrah et al., 2009; Rao et al., 2012; Ghedin et al., 2009; Taylor et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on doxycycline treatment.

claim: Long treatment times and contraindications for children and pregnant women limit the suitability of antibiotic treatment for mass-drug administration efforts.
source: While antibiotic treatment remains a viable option for individual patients, long treatment times and contraindications for children and pregnant women limit its suitability for mass-drug administration efforts (Taylor et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research on antibiotic treatment limitations.

claim: Rifampicin may possess filaricidal activity, but these data are preliminary and have not yet been tested in humans.
source: This strategy is ongoing, as recent evidence suggests that the commonly used antibiotic rifampicin may also possess filaricidal activity, but these data are preliminary and have not yet been tested in humans (Aljayyoussi et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to recent research on rifampicin.

claim: Bioinformatic identification of essential pathways as drug targets has been successfully demonstrated against many pathogens, including nematodes.
source: The bioinformatic identification of essential pathways as drug targets has been successfully demonstrated against many pathogens, including nematodes (Taylor et al., 2013a), Entamoeba histolytica (Klebanov and Yakovlev, 2007), Plasmodium falciparum (Yeh et al., 2004; Fatumo et al., 2009; Chiappino-Pepe et al., 2017), and various bacterial pathogens (Rahman and Schomburg, 2006; Kim et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on bioinformatic drug target identification.

claim: Genome scale metabolic reconstruction and constraint-based modeling have emerged as effective strategies to identify critical metabolic enzymes and pathways.
source: Genome scale metabolic reconstruction and constraint-based modeling in particular have emerged as effective strategies to identify critical metabolic enzymes and pathways (Oberhardt et al., 2008; Chavali et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2009; Song et al., 2013), which, due to their importance in energy production and in generating the building blocks required for growth and survival, are good potential therapeutic targets (Cotton et al., 2016; Chiappino-Pepe et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on metabolic modeling.

claim: Metabolic enzymes and pathways are good potential therapeutic targets due to their importance in energy production and generating building blocks for growth and survival.
source: Genome scale metabolic reconstruction and constraint-based modeling in particular have emerged as effective strategies to identify critical metabolic enzymes and pathways (Oberhardt et al., 2008; Chavali et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2009; Song et al., 2013), which, due to their importance in energy production and in generating the building blocks required for growth and survival, are good potential therapeutic targets (Cotton et al., 2016; Chiappino-Pepe et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research and established knowledge about metabolic pathways.

claim: iDC625 contains 1266 total reactions involving 1252 total metabolites.
source: The final reconstruction, designated iDC625, contains 1266 total reactions involving 1252 total metabolites.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from the metabolic reconstruction.

claim: Of the 1266 reactions in iDC625, 1011 represent enzymes of which 849 are associated with 625 genes.
source: Of the 1266 reactions, 1011 represent enzymes of which 849 are associated with 625 genes; 575 of these enzymatic reactions are associated with the cytosolic compartment, 166 with the mitochondria, and 270 with Wolbachia (Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 1 showing the network representation.

claim: 575 enzymatic reactions are associated with the cytosolic compartment, 166 with the mitochondria, and 270 with Wolbachia.
source: Of the 1266 reactions, 1011 represent enzymes of which 849 are associated with 625 genes; 575 of these enzymatic reactions are associated with the cytosolic compartment, 166 with the mitochondria, and 270 with Wolbachia (Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 1 showing the compartmentalized network.

claim: 226 reactions are associated with transport across compartments in iDC625.
source: Of the remaining reactions, 226 are associated with transport across compartments, of which 37 represent metabolite exchange between the mitochondria and cytosol, 80 between Wolbachia and the cytosol, and the remaining 109 representing metabolite exchange between the cytosol and the extracellular milieu.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from the metabolic reconstruction.

claim: The 1011 enzymatic reactions in iDC625 represent 761 unique KEGG reactions.
source: After filtering compartmental duplicates, the 1011 enzymatic reactions represent 761 unique KEGG reactions.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from the metabolic reconstruction.

claim: 319 (42%) of the KEGG reactions in iDC625 are unique to B. malayi and 442 (58%) are shared with iCEL1273.
source: For context, the C. elegans metabolic reconstruction iCEL1273 (Yilmaz and Walhout, 2016) contains 1985 total reactions representing 929 unique KEGG reactions; a comparison between these sets indicates that 319 (42%) of the KEGG reactions are unique to B. malayi and 442 (58%) are shared with iCEL1273.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from comparative analysis with the C. elegans model.

claim: The 1252 metabolites in iDC625 represent 1025 unique KEGG metabolites, of which 602 (59%) are unique to B. malayi and 423 (41%) are shared with iCEL1273.
source: These represent 1025 unique KEGG metabolites, of which 602 (59%) are unique to B. malayi and 423 (41%) are shared with iCEL1273.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from comparative analysis with the C. elegans model.

claim: 87.6% of the B. malayi genes and 96.4% of the Wolbachia genes were expressed in at least one life stage.
source: In total, we obtained relative expression data for 11,840 B. malayi and 823 Wolbachia genes across ten different life-stages; 87.6% of the B. malayi genes and 96.4% of the Wolbachia genes were expressed in at least one stage.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from transcriptomic analysis.

claim: The maximum production of the biomass objective function occurs at Wolbachia weights of 0.04, 0.02, 0.02, and 0.01 under HOHG, HOLG, LOHG, and LOLG conditions, respectively.
source: By applying these constraints to the otherwise unconstrained model and varying the relative weight of Wolbachia, we found that the maximum production of the biomass objective function occurs at Wolbachia weights of 0.04, 0.02, 0.02, and 0.01 under HOHG, HOLG, LOHG, and LOLG, respectively (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 2 showing the relationship between Wolbachia weight and biomass production.

claim: A Wolbachia weight of 0.1 was assigned under all nutrient conditions to minimize the impact on the objective function while being conservative.
source: Since the negative impact to the objective function was minimal until 0.18, we assigned a weight of 0.1 under all nutrient conditions. This was chosen to minimize the impact on the objective function, while still being conservative in allowing reasonable flux through Wolbachia reactions.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents a methodological decision based on model performance data.

claim: The model predicts that Wolbachia populations expanded in adult male B. pahangi worms when supplemented with exogenous pyruvate.
source: With this in mind, we attempted to validate our models against a previous finding that Wolbachia populations expanded in adult male B. pahangi worms when supplemented with exogenous pyruvate (Voronin et al., 2019; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research and model validation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: At a Wolbachia weight of 1.0, the objective function averaged over HOHG, HOLG, LOHG, and LOLG increased for all life stage models when excess pyruvate was made available.
source: At a Wolbachia weight of 1.0, the objective function averaged over HOHG, HOLG, LOHG, and LOLG increased for all life stage models when excess pyruvate was made available (Supplementary file 1-supplemental table 1: 'The objective flux under a high Wolbachia weight').
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by data in Supplementary file 1.

claim: The increase in objective function with excess pyruvate was largest in the three adult male models (10.3%), compared to adult females (6.16%), the larval stages (7.20%), or the unconstrained model (5.88%).
source: The increase was largest in the three adult male models (10.3%), compared to adult females (6.16%), the larval stages (7.20%), or the unconstrained model (5.88%).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations with excess pyruvate.

claim: pFBA predicts a reliance on anaerobic pathways under low oxygen conditions.
source: As expected, pFBA predicts a reliance on anaerobic pathways under low oxygen conditions (Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 3 showing pathway activities under different oxygen conditions.

claim: At an oxygen concentration of 205 flux units, there is a switch to the aerobic pathway in the unconstrained and L3 models.
source: However, at an oxygen concentration of 205 flux units (Figure 3, vertical-dashed line), there is a switch to the aerobic pathway in the unconstrained and L3 models.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 3 showing the anaerobic-aerobic threshold.

claim: The acetate and propanoate waste transporters are no longer used above the oxygen threshold of 205 flux units.
source: Interestingly, the acetate and propanoate waste transporters are no longer used above this threshold; the predicted presence of these waste products is consistent with previous studies of helminth anaerobic metabolism (Tielens et al., 2010; Müller et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations to previous research on helminth metabolism.

claim: The model produces the most biomass under HOHG conditions.
source: We observe that the model produces the most biomass under HOHG conditions, as expected.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations.

claim: Under HOHG conditions, the model predicts a reliance on the glyoxylate shunt to produce malate and succinate.
source: Instead of using the full TCA cycle, the model predicts a reliance on the glyoxylate shunt to produce malate and succinate (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 4 showing the metabolic pathways.

claim: Under HOHG conditions, 74.6% of malate is processed by the TCA cycle to isocitrate which is recycled back into the glyoxylate shunt.
source: A large proportion (74.6%) of malate is processed by the TCA cycle to isocitrate which is recycled back into the glyoxylate shunt, and 18.2% is predicted to be processed through anaerobic pathways to produce succinate, a phenomenon termed the Crabtree effect (Postma et al., 1989; Pfeiffer and Morley, 2014), in which anaerobic pathways are used by the cell in the presence of high oxygen and glucose.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations under HOHG conditions.

claim: Under HOHG conditions, 18.2% of malate is predicted to be processed through anaerobic pathways to produce succinate, a phenomenon termed the Crabtree effect.
source: A large proportion (74.6%) of malate is processed by the TCA cycle to isocitrate which is recycled back into the glyoxylate shunt, and 18.2% is predicted to be processed through anaerobic pathways to produce succinate, a phenomenon termed the Crabtree effect (Postma et al., 1989; Pfeiffer and Morley, 2014), in which anaerobic pathways are used by the cell in the presence of high oxygen and glucose.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations to previous research on the Crabtree effect.

claim: Under HOHG conditions, 74.5% of the oxygen imported is used to generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation.
source: The majority of the oxygen imported (74.5%) is used to generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation, while only 6.2% (36 units) is predicted to be used by Wolbachia.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations under HOHG conditions.

claim: Under HOHG conditions, only 6.2% (36 units) of oxygen is predicted to be used by Wolbachia.
source: The majority of the oxygen imported (74.5%) is used to generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation, while only 6.2% (36 units) is predicted to be used by Wolbachia.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations under HOHG conditions.

claim: Under HOLG conditions, growth is predicted to fall to 82% of optimal biomass production.
source: Under HOLG conditions, growth is predicted to fall to 82% of optimal biomass production.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations under HOLG conditions.

claim: Under HOLG conditions, 71.2% of the oxygen is used for oxidative phosphorylation in the mitochondria, while 6.0% (35 units) is used by Wolbachia.
source: Similar to HOHG, 71.2% of the oxygen is used for oxidative phosphorylation in the mitochondria, while 6.0% (35 units) is used by Wolbachia.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations under HOLG conditions.

claim: Under LOHG conditions, biomass production falls to 69%.
source: Under LOHG conditions, biomass production falls to 69%.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations under LOHG conditions.

claim: Under LOHG conditions, the glycolytic pathway is used to generate energy, with glucose metabolized to phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) producing approximately half of the total NADH used by the model.
source: Here, the glycolytic pathway is used to generate energy, with glucose metabolized to phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) producing approximately half of the total NADH used by the model, which is then transported into the mitochondria via the malate-aspartate shuttle.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations under LOHG conditions.

claim: Under LOHG conditions, 61.0% of the oxygen is used to generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation, while 37.8% (34 units) is used by Wolbachia.
source: Under these conditions, most of the oxygen in the model (61.0%) is used to generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation, while 37.8% (34 units) is used by Wolbachia.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations under LOHG conditions.

claim: Under LOLG conditions biomass production is reduced to 37% of the optimal.
source: Under LOLG conditions biomass production is reduced to 37% of the optimal.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations under LOLG conditions.

claim: Under LOLG conditions, 69.8% of the oxygen is being consumed by oxidative phosphorylation, and 29.6% (27 units) is used by Wolbachia.
source: Under these conditions 69.8% of the oxygen is being consumed by oxidative phosphorylation, and 29.6% (27 units) is used by Wolbachia.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations under LOLG conditions.

claim: The model predicts a potentially novel form of glutamate metabolism, representing a combination of the malate-aspartate shuttle and the TCA cycle.
source: Interestingly, the model predicts a potentially novel form of glutamate metabolism, representing a combination of the malate-aspartate shuttle and the TCA cycle (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 4 showing the metabolic pathways.

claim: The novel glutamate metabolic pathway results in the conversion of glutamate to aspartate and CO2, along with the production of GTP, 2 x NADH, and ubiquinone.
source: The net reaction results in the conversion of glutamate to aspartate and CO2, along with the production of key energy metabolites: GTP, 2 x NADH, and ubiquinone.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations.

claim: The novel glutamate metabolic pathway is almost equivalent to the energy produced by the catabolism of a single molecule of acetyl CoA by the TCA cycle.
source: This is almost equivalent to the energy produced by the catabolism of a single molecule of acetyl CoA by the TCA cycle: 2 x CO2, GTP, 3 x NADH, and ubiquinone.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents an inference from model data.

claim: The novel glutamate metabolic pathway has a striking resemblance to the catabolism used by intestinal epithelial cells and to the 'glutamine addiction' pathway used by many cancer cells.
source: However, the striking resemblance to the catabolism used by intestinal epithelial cells (Blachier et al., 2009) and to the relatively recently described 'glutamine addiction' pathway used by many cancer cells (Wise and Thompson, 2010; Mazat and Ransac, 2019) suggests it may be physiologically relevant.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations to previous research on similar metabolic pathways.

claim: Wolbachia may function to supplement mitochondrial energy production in filarial nematodes.
source: It has previously been suggested that Wolbachia may function to supplement mitochondrial energy production in filarial nematodes (Darby et al., 2012); our model predictions support this hypothesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research and model predictions.

claim: Under LOLG conditions, Wolbachia is predicted to export the maximum amount of ATP possible (100 units) into the B. malayi cytosol.
source: Under LOLG conditions, Wolbachia is predicted to export the maximum amount of ATP possible (100 units) into the B. malayi cytosol.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations under LOLG conditions.

claim: Under LOLG conditions, pyruvate import by Wolbachia is nearly zero, and Wolbachia is using the novel glutamate metabolic pathway.
source: It was also suggested that Wolbachia uses pyruvate as its primary carbon source (Voronin et al., 2016), but under LOLG conditions pyruvate import is nearly zero, and Wolbachia is using the novel glutamate metabolic pathway described above.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations under LOLG conditions, contrasting with a previous hypothesis.

claim: Under LOHG conditions, Wolbachia ATP export drops to 90% compared to LOLG conditions.
source: Under LOHG conditions, Wolbachia ATP export drops to 90% compared to LOLG conditions.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations under LOHG conditions.

claim: Under LOHG conditions, pyruvate import by Wolbachia increases substantially (nine units instead of 1), and the model uses both the TCA cycle and the glutamate metabolic pathway to generate energy.
source: Pyruvate import increases substantially (nine units instead of 1), and the model uses both the TCA cycle and the glutamate metabolic pathway to generate energy.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations under LOHG conditions.

claim: The models produced the most biomass under HOHG conditions, and the unconstrained (open) model produced the most under all conditions.
source: As expected, the models produced the most biomass under HOHG conditions, and the unconstrained (open) model produced the most under all conditions.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations across different conditions.

claim: There was little difference under LOLG conditions between any of the models, except for adult worms at 120 dpi (M120 and F120).
source: There was little difference under LOLG conditions between any of the models, except for adult worms at 120 dpi (M120 and F120).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations under LOLG conditions.

claim: The L3 model experiences a large benefit under LOHG or HOLG conditions compared to LOLG, but there is no increased benefit when moving from either to HOHG conditions.
source: While the L3 model experiences a large benefit under LOHG or HOLG conditions compared to LOLG, there is no increased benefit when moving from either to HOHG conditions.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations for the L3 stage.

claim: The M120 model appears to be saturated for glucose and oxygen even under LOLG conditions, as its biomass production never increases when more of either nutrient is made available.
source: The M120 model appears to be saturated for these nutrients even under LOLG conditions, as its biomass production never increases when more of either nutrient is made available.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations for the M120 stage.

claim: The F120 model appears to be nearly saturated and receives only a modest benefit from additional glucose or oxygen.
source: The F120 model appears to be nearly saturated and receives only a modest benefit from additional glucose or oxygen.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from model simulations for the F120 stage.

claim: The Wolbachia compartment changes the least among the different models and conditions, while the mitochondrial compartment shows the most variation.
source: We found that the Wolbachia compartment changes the least among the different models and conditions, while the mitochondrial compartment shows the most variation.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from analysis of reaction usage across models.

claim: Both the L3D6 and L3D9 models appear to be substantially more enzymatically constrained than L3.
source: It is interesting to note that both the L3D6 and L3D9 models appear to be substantially more enzymatically constrained than L3.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from analysis of reaction usage in molting stages.

claim: The reduced usage numbers and reduced biomass production in L3D6 and L3D9 may reflect the specialized function and large energetic expenditure of molting.
source: These reduced usage numbers, combined with reduced biomass production (Figure 5), may reflect this specialized function and large energetic expenditure.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents an inference from model data about molting stages.

claim: Untargeted metabolomics identified 146 unique metabolites from a 'hybrid' analysis and 492 from a 'predictive' analysis.
source: Applying two complementary approaches, our analyses identified 146 unique metabolites from a 'hybrid' analysis and 492 from a 'predictive' analysis (see Materials and methods for details); of these, 103 and 316 metabolites were found in at least three samples, respectively.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from metabolomics analysis.

claim: 103 metabolites from the hybrid analysis and 316 from the predictive analysis were found in at least three samples.
source: Applying two complementary approaches, our analyses identified 146 unique metabolites from a 'hybrid' analysis and 492 from a 'predictive' analysis (see Materials and methods for details); of these, 103 and 316 metabolites were found in at least three samples, respectively.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from metabolomics analysis.

claim: Most of the TCA cycle intermediates were detected in one or both metabolomics data sets.
source: Most of the TCA cycle intermediates (Figure 4) were detected in one or both of our metabolomics data sets.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from metabolomics analysis.

claim: Carnitine and acetylcarnitine were detected in all samples in both analyses and were found to be highest in males, followed by females, microfilaria, and finally L3.
source: Carnitine and acetylcarnitine were detected in all samples in both analyses and were found to be highest in males, followed by females, microfilaria, and finally L3.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from metabolomics analysis.

claim: A general trend of the highest metabolic activity in the adults (in particular males metabolizing fatty acids), followed by the microfilaria, with L3 having the lowest levels was observed.
source: If we accept that higher levels of these intermediates imply increased metabolic activity, then we observe a general trend of the highest activity in the adults (in particular males metabolizing fatty acids), followed by the microfilaria, with L3 having the lowest levels if any were detected.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents an inference from metabolomics data.

claim: L3 is a non-feeding stage, which has been likened to the dauer stage of C. elegans.
source: This fits with the observation that L3 is a non-feeding stage, which has been likened to the dauer stage of C. elegans (Li et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research on L3 biology.

claim: Of the 1011 enzymatic reactions in iDC625, 815 had no impact on the biomass objective function when knocked out.
source: Of the 1011 enzymatic reactions in iDC625, 815 had no impact on the biomass objective function when knocked out (Figure 7A), 94 were found to have a low impact (biomass ≥50% of baseline), and 102 were found to be essential (biomass <50% of baseline).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 7A showing the breakdown of reaction essentiality.

claim: 94 reactions were found to have a low impact (biomass ≥50% of baseline) when knocked out.
source: Of the 1011 enzymatic reactions in iDC625, 815 had no impact on the biomass objective function when knocked out (Figure 7A), 94 were found to have a low impact (biomass ≥50% of baseline), and 102 were found to be essential (biomass <50% of baseline).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 7A showing the breakdown of reaction essentiality.

claim: 102 reactions were found to be essential (biomass <50% of baseline) when knocked out.
source: Of the 1011 enzymatic reactions in iDC625, 815 had no impact on the biomass objective function when knocked out (Figure 7A), 94 were found to have a low impact (biomass ≥50% of baseline), and 102 were found to be essential (biomass <50% of baseline).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 7A showing the breakdown of reaction essentiality.

claim: The set of essential reactions was quite robust to changes in model conditions.
source: This set of essential reactions was generated under HOHG conditions, but proved to be quite robust to the model conditions.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from sensitivity analysis of essential reactions.

claim: Increasing the Wolbachia weight from 0.1 to 0.5 decreased the maximum biomass production by ~20% but had no effect on the reactions predicted as essential.
source: Increasing the Wolbachia weight from 0.1 to 0.5 decreased the maximum biomass production by ~20% but had no effect on the reactions predicted as essential, and even increasing it to 0.9 only reclassified one reaction as non-essential (KEGG reaction R07618 from the Wolbachia compartment).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from sensitivity analysis of essential reactions.

claim: There were only 14 essential reactions shared by iCEL1273 and iDC625.
source: There were only 14 essential reactions shared by iCEL1273 and iDC625 (Figure 7B), but this low overlap is likely because both sets of model predictions are missing many biologically essential reactions.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 7B showing the Venn diagram of essential reactions.

claim: 73% of the predicted iDC625 essential reactions overlap with the experimentally determined essential reactions of C. elegans.
source: This is suggested by the large significant overlap between each model's predictions and the experimentally determined essential reactions; even though they are separated by 400 million years of evolution and possess different life cycle strategies (parasitic v free-living), 73% of the predicted iDC625 essential reactions overlap with the experimentally determined essential reactions of C. elegans (significance determined by one-tailed Fisher's Exact Test; hypergeometric p-value = 1.9E−11).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents data from comparative analysis with C. elegans experimental data.

claim: 129 reactions were involved in at least one pair of knockouts that together reduced biomass production to less than 50%.
source: Of the 909 reactions which were predicted to inhibit growth by less than 50% when knocked out individually, 129 were involved in at least one pair of knockouts that together reduced biomass production to less than 50% (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 7C showing the synthetic lethal interactions.

claim: The model possesses alternative pathways to produce nicotinate, and knocking out different combinations of these pathways had a dramatic impact on biomass production.
source: Analyses reveal that the model possesses alternative pathways to produce nicotinate—important in redox reactions—and that knocking out different combinations of these pathways had a dramatic impact on biomass production (Figure 7C; P1, P2, P3, and P11).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 7C showing the synthetic lethal interactions.

claim: The loss of one half of the TCA cycle or the other can be compensated for by the model, but not both, and only if the Wolbachia TCA cycle is functional.
source: Our simulations also predict that the loss of one half of the TCA cycle or the other can be compensated for by the model, but not both, and only if the Wolbachia TCA cycle is functional (Figure 7C; P4, P5, P6, and P15).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 7C showing the synthetic lethal interactions.

claim: Pyrimidine biosynthesis pathways are only predicted as essential through synthetic lethal interactions, suggesting redundancy in these pathways.
source: While purine biosynthesis pathways are predicted to be essential by our in silico single knockouts, pyrimidine biosynthesis pathways are only predicted as essential through synthetic lethal interactions, suggesting redundancy in these pathways (Figure 7C; P7, P8, P9, and P10).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 7C showing the synthetic lethal interactions.

claim: The model is the first to incorporate the anaerobic metabolic pathway used by parasitic nematodes.
source: Our model is the first to incorporate this pathway and is therefore likely to yield accurate predictions as low oxygen environments are biologically relevant for parasitic nematodes.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents a novel contribution of the model.

claim: The Crabtree effect occurs only under conditions that result in succinate export.
source: It is interesting to note that succinate export flux mirrors the activity pattern of fumarase (Figure 3), potentially indicating that the Crabtree effect occurs only under conditions that result in succinate export.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and represents an inference from model data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The glyoxylate pathway is widely accepted to be functional in nematodes and is regarded as a conduit from fatty acids to glucose during embryogenesis.
source: The relevant genes have been detected in several Metazoan species, but the nematodes are the only group where the pathway is widely accepted to be functional, and where it is regarded as a conduit from fatty acids to glucose during embryogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about the glyoxylate pathway in nematodes.

claim: The glyoxylate pathway may play a role in energy metabolism, particularly when metabolizing fatty acids.
source: It has been suggested that this pathway may also play a role in energy metabolism (Butler et al., 2012)—in particular when metabolizing fatty acids—and our results appear to support that this hypothesis is plausible.

claim: Previous predictions of essentiality based on the iCEL1273 C. elegans model were broadly consistent with in vitro gene essentiality screens.
source: Previous predictions of essentiality based on a compartmentalized model of C. elegans metabolism, iCEL1273, were broadly consistent with in vitro gene essentiality screens (Yilmaz and Walhout, 2016), suggesting the process by which we made our predictions is likely to be biologically relevant.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research on the C. elegans model.
